parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Genetic technology involving the creation of recombinant DNA can be used to treat different human diseases. These include diseases such as diabetes that may have multiple causes and inherited disorders that are caused by a single gene.

Outline **two different** ways of using recombinant DNA technology to treat these diseases.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A new application of recombinant DNA technology uses the genetic modification of a plant to prevent disease. It aims to prevent the most common source of food-borne disease, which is caused by eating food contaminated with pathogenic *Escherichia coli* bacteria.

Scientists genetically modified edible spinach plants to produce colicins. Colicins are antimicrobial proteins that can kill pathogenic *E.coli*. Colicins are normally made by other bacteria.

An experiment was carried out to test this application by spraying an extract of genetically modified (GM) spinach in buffer solution onto raw meat contaminated with pathogenic *E.coli*. The meat was stored at $10^\circ\text{C}$ for varying lengths of time before the numbers of viable (living) pathogenic *E.coli* bacteria were counted. Fig. 4.1 shows the results.
{{figure:figure_4_1.webp}}
Fig. 4.1
parts.text: With reference to Fig. 4.1, evaluate the effectiveness of using GM spinach spray on raw meat to prevent food-borne disease.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
Regulatory authorities may not approve the use of GM spinach spray on raw meat to protect consumers.

Discuss the concerns that may stop regulatory authorities approving this application of recombinant DNA technology.
